text: Hypothesised causes: prevalence in training text, and human RLHF reviewers rating the construction highly because it signals nuance and insight. Nobody, including model makers, is sure; OpenAI's model-behavior staff prefer the label 'contrastive phrasing'. (medium confidence)

Reader-side harm: cognitive-psychology work cited by The Conversation says negation does not erase the negated concept; readers process it first and often lose the negation tag, so the pattern plants the strawman it denies. (medium confidence)
Suggested fix: lead with what the thing is, drop the defensive strawman, and use a contrast only when it is specific and non-obvious. (medium confidence)
Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing lists negative parallelism ("Not only X but Y", "It is not just X, it's Y", "no X, no Y, just Z") as an LLM tell. (high confidence)

Wikipedia states LLMs use negative parallelism about three times more frequently than humans; the article rests on a single source, Will Oremus's 2026 Atlantic piece, and carries a single-source maintenance notice. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)
The Atlantic (via AI Weekly summary) reports Barron's counted the phrase in Fortune 500 filings rising from 50 in 2023 to over 200 in 2025. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

Humans use the device too (listicles, ad copy, speeches); Wikipedia says isolated instances are not conclusive and it must be corroborated by other signs. The tell is frequency and repetition within a text. (high confidence)
